It remains to relate Is~∗​(x,c,Φ,πU)I^{*}_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U}) and Is~​(x,c,Φ,πU)I_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U}). Recall that the quantities mρ​(s,a)m_{\rho}(s,a) and mρΨ​(s,a)m_{\rho}^{\Psi}(s,a) appearing in [24] correspond in our notation to ωΦ,πU​(s,a)\omega_{\Phi,\pi_{U}}(s,a) and ωΨ,πU​(s,a)\omega_{\Psi,\pi_{U}}(s,a), respectively. As noted at the start of [24, Appendix D.3.3], ωΦ,πU​(s,a)∼ωΨ,πU​(s,a)\omega_{\Phi,\pi_{U}}(s,a)\sim\omega_{\Psi,\pi_{U}}(s,a). It follows that (i)(i) there exists some constant 𝔡1>0\mathfrak{d}_{1}>0 that is independent of nn such that for all sufficiently large nn, ωΦ,πU​(s,a)/ωΨ,πU​(s,a)≤(1/𝔡1)\omega_{\Phi,\pi_{U}}(s,a)/\allowbreak\omega_{\Psi,\pi_{U}}(s,a)\leq(1/\mathfrak{d}_{1}) for all ss and aa.

Moreover, upon expanding the KL-divergence appearing in (13) one finds that Is~​(x,c,Φ,πU)I_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U}) is linear in ωΨ,πU\omega_{\Psi,\pi_{U}}. Likewise, Is~∗​(x,c,Φ,πU)I^{*}_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U}) is linear in ωΦ,πU\omega_{\Phi,\pi_{U}}. Together with point (i)(i) this implies that Is~​(x,c,Φ,πU)≥𝔡1​Is~∗​(x,c,Φ,πU)I_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U})\geq\mathfrak{d}_{1}I^{*}_{\tilde{s}}(x;c,\Phi,\pi_{U}) for all sufficiently large nn, from which the result now follows. ∎

D.2 Proof of Proposition 5.3

Recall that Tk=k​HT_{k}=kH. Let

k∗:=max⁡{k′>0:Tk′≤Θclust}k^{*}\vcentcolon=\max\{k^{\prime}>0:T_{k^{\prime}}\leq\Theta^{\textnormal{clust}}\} (202)

be the number of episodes belonging to the first phase of Algorithm 1. Because we assumed Θclust=ω⁡(n​A​(S3+ln⁡n))\Theta^{\textnormal{clust}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}+\ln n)) and n=Ω⁡(H)n=\Omega(H), it follows that Tk∗≥Θclust−H=ω⁡(n​A​(S3+ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}\geq\Theta^{\textnormal{clust}}-H=\omega(nA(S^{3}+\ln n)). Recall also that f^0\hat{f}_{0} denotes the output of [24, Algorithm 1], and that f^ℓ\hat{f}_{\ell} for ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0 are the intermediate iterates of [24, Algorithm 2]. The final estimator is f^alg=f^⌈ln⁡n⌉\hat{f}^{\textnormal{alg}}=\hat{f}_{\lceil\ln n\rceil}.

Following [24], as well as [44, 35], the proof consists of two steps. First, we bound the number of misclassifications made by f^0\hat{f}_{0}. Then, we show that the successive iterates f^ℓ\hat{f}_{\ell} eliminate these errors so that f^⌈ln⁡n⌉\hat{f}_{\lceil\ln n\rceil} achieves exact recovery. These steps correspond to [24, Theorems 2 and 3], respectively.

Two preliminary reductions will allow us to adapt and streamline the analysis for our setting:

  1. 1.

    Throughout [24], it is assumed that I⁡(Φ)=Ω⁡(1)I(\Phi)=\Omega(1). We do not directly assume this, but it remains true under the assumptions of Lemma 5.1; see Appendix B.

  2. 2.

    The trimming step in [24, Algorithm 1] is unnecessary in our regime. Because Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3+ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}+\ln n)), for sufficiently large nn, Γa=[n]\Gamma_{a}=[n] for a∈[A]a\in[A]. We assume throughout the proof that nn is large enough for this to be the case.

To avoid unnecessary repetition, we refer to [24] wherever arguments are unchanged. We thus highlight only the adaptations necessary for our setting. We therefore ask you to keep [24], and in particular [24, Appendix F and G], on the side while reading onwards.

Step 1: Bounding |ℰ⁡(f^0,f)||\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{0},f)|

Recall (11). The number of misclassifications |ℰ⁡(f^0,f)||\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{0},f)| of f^0\hat{f}_{0} is bounded in [24, Theorem 2], which is a consequence of the refined statement in [24, Theorem 11]. We inspect the proof of [24, Theorem 11] to identify the event on which the implication of [24, Theorem 2] is true.

Recall (39) and (40), and recall from Section A.1 that 𝐍^a=(N^k∗+1​(x,a,y))x,y∈[n]∈ℝn×n\hat{\mathbf{N}}_{a}=(\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}(x,a,y))_{x,y\in[n]}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} for a∈[A]a\in[A]. Let 𝐍a:=(∑k′∈[k]∑h=1HN~a,k′,h​(x,y))x,y∈[n]\mathbf{N}_{a}\vcentcolon=(\sum_{k^{\prime}\in[k]}\sum_{h=1}^{H}\allowbreak\tilde{N}_{a,k^{\prime},h}(x,y))_{x,y\in[n]}, where the N~a,k′,h​(x,y)\tilde{N}_{a,k^{\prime},h}(x,y) are defined at the start of [24, Appendix F.1] as N~a,k′,h(x,y):=ℙ[xk′,h=x,ak′,h=a,xk′,h+1=y∣xk′,h−2]\tilde{N}_{a,k^{\prime},h}(x,y)\vcentcolon=\mathbb{P}[x_{k^{\prime},h}=x,a_{k^{\prime},h}=a,x_{k^{\prime},h+1}=y\mid x_{k^{\prime},h-2}] if h>2h>2 and N~a,k′,h​(x,y):=ℙ⁡[xk′,h=x,ak′,h=a,xk′,h+1=y]\tilde{N}_{a,k^{\prime},h}(x,y)\vcentcolon=\mathbb{P}[x_{k^{\prime},h}=x,a_{k^{\prime},h}=a,x_{k^{\prime},h+1}=y] otherwise. Finally, let ∥⋅∥\lVert\,\cdot\rVert denote the spectral norm for matrices.

Observe that because Γa=[n]\Gamma_{a}=[n] by reduction (2) above, the matrix 𝐍^Γ,a\hat{\mathbf{N}}_{\Gamma,a}, obtained from 𝐍^\hat{\mathbf{N}} by setting to zero all rows and columns corresponding to contexts not in Γa\Gamma_{a}, equals 𝐍^a\hat{\mathbf{N}}_{a}.

Identifying

N^a​(x,y)≡N^k∗+1​(x,a,y),T​H≡Tk∗,\hat{N}_{a}(x,y)\equiv\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}(x,a,y),\quad TH\equiv T_{k^{*}}, (203)

it now follows from the final step in the proof of [24, Theorem 11] that there exists a constant 𝔠2>0\mathfrak{c}_{2}>0 such that for any 𝔠1>0\mathfrak{c}_{1}>0

Ω1:={maxa∥𝐍^a−𝐍a∥≤𝔠1Tk∗n​A}⊂{|ℰ⁡(f^0,f)|n≤𝔠1𝔠2n​S​ATk∗}.\Omega_{1}\vcentcolon=\biggl\{\max_{a}\lVert\hat{\mathbf{N}}_{a}-\mathbf{N}_{a}\rVert\leq\mathfrak{c}_{1}\sqrt{\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}\biggr\}\subset\biggl\{\frac{|\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{0},f)|}{n}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{1}\mathfrak{c}_{2}\sqrt{\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}}\biggr\}. (204)

We note here that the right-hand side is the event whose probability is bounded by [24, Theorem 2], and that Ω1\Omega_{1} is the event whose probability is bounded by [24, Proposition 19]. The latter states that there exists 𝔠1>0\mathfrak{c}_{1}>0 such that

ℙ⁡[Ω1]≥1−2n−2​e−n−2​e−Tk∗n​A=1−O⁡(1n),\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{1}]\geq 1-\frac{2}{n}-2e^{-n}-2e^{-\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}=1-O\biggl(\frac{1}{n}\biggr), (205)

where equality follows from Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)) as is assumed in Proposition 5.3. We will now explain how (205) can be refined to 1−O⁡(1/nc)1-O(1/n^{c}) for arbitrary c>0c>0 by choosing constant 𝔠1\mathfrak{c}_{1} sufficiently large.

The proof of [24, Proposition 19] bounds maxa⁡∥𝐍^a−𝐍a∥\max_{a}\lVert\hat{\mathbf{N}}_{a}-\mathbf{N}_{a}\rVert by three terms labeled T1T_{1}, T2T_{2}, and T3T_{3}. These are subsequently bounded in [24, (75)–(77)]. To show that ℙ⁡[Ω1]=1−O⁡(1/nc)\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{1}]=1-O(1/n^{c}) it suffices to improve the probability bound in [24, (77)], which is a consequence of [24, Lemma 18]. [24, Lemma 18] is proven by showing that a particular random matrix QQ, defined therein, satisfies a discrepancy property33 3 A matrix QQ is said to be discrepant if there exist constants ξ1,ξ2>0\xi_{1},\xi_{2}>0 such that for every ℐ,𝒥⊂[n]\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J}\subset[n], e⁡(ℐ,𝒥):=∑(x,y)∈ℐ×𝒥Q⁡(x,y)e(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J})\vcentcolon=\sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal{I}\times\mathcal{J}}Q(x,y) satisfies either e⁡(ℐ,𝒥)​n2​A/(|ℐ|​|𝒥|​Tk∗)≤ξ1e(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J})n^{2}A/(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{J}|T_{k^{*}})\leq\xi_{1} or e⁡(ℐ,𝒥)​ln⁡(e⁡(ℐ,𝒥)​n2​A/(|ℐ|​|𝒥|​Tk∗))≤ξ2​(|ℐ|∨|𝒥|)​ln⁡(n/(|ℐ|∨|𝒥|))e(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J})\ln(e(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J})n^{2}A/(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{J}|T_{k^{*}}))\leq\xi_{2}(|\mathcal{I}|\vee|\mathcal{J}|)\ln(n/(|\mathcal{I}|\vee|\mathcal{J}|)). with high probability as n→∞n\rightarrow\infty.

To prove that QQ is discrepant, [24] separately considers the cases |𝒥|>n/5|\mathcal{J}|>n/5 and |𝒥|≤n/5|\mathcal{J}|\leq n/5. The case |𝒥|>n/5|\mathcal{J}|>n/5 does not require modification. When |𝒥|≤n/5|\mathcal{J}|\leq n/5, it is shown that QQ is discrepant whenever a certain event ℰ\mathcal{E}, whose definition we do not reproduce here, holds. The probability bound for ℰc\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{c}} contributes the term 2/n2/n in (205), which we now show can be improved to 2/nc2/n^{c} for any c>0c>0 by allowing QQ to be discrepant for a larger constant ξ2\xi_{2}. The latter ultimately leads to a larger constant 𝔠1\mathfrak{c}_{1} in (204). This tradeoff was also exploited in, e.g., [21, 5] in the context of random graphs and in [43] for BMCs.

Specifically, it is shown in the proof of [24, Lemma 18] that

ℙ⁡[ℰ]≥1−∑1≤i≤j≤n/52​exp⁡((4−ξ2)​j​ln⁡(n/j)).\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]\geq 1-\sum_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n/5}2\exp((4-\xi_{2})j\ln(n/j)). (206)

The constant ξ2\xi_{2} is then chosen as ξ2=7+ln⁡A/ln⁡n\xi_{2}=7+\ln A/\ln n, which leads to ℙ⁡[ℰ]≥1−2/(n​A)\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]\geq 1-2/(nA).

To show that ℙ⁡[Ω1]=1−O⁡(1/nc)\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{1}]=1-O(1/n^{c}) instead, it suffices to choose ξ2\xi_{2} large enough that ℙ⁡[ℰ]=1−O⁡(1/(nc​A))\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]=1-O(1/(n^{c}A)). This can be done for any fixed c>0c>0 by choosing ξ2=6+c+ln⁡A/ln⁡n\xi_{2}=6+c+\ln A/\ln n. Note that Proposition 5.3’s hypothesis that A=nO⁡(1)A=n^{O(1)} ensures that ξ2\xi_{2} is indeed upper bounded by a constant for sufficiently large nn. Substitution of this choice into (206) yields

ℙ⁡[ℰ]≥1−∑1≤i≤j≤n/52​exp⁡(−(2+c+ln⁡A/ln⁡n)​j​ln⁡(n/j))​≥(i)​1−2​n2​(1n)2+c+ln⁡A/ln⁡n=1−2nc​A,\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]\geq 1-\sum_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n/5}2\exp(-(2+c+\ln A/\ln n)j\ln(n/j))\overset{(i)}{\geq}1-2n^{2}\biggl(\frac{1}{n}\biggr)^{2+c+\ln A/\ln n}=1-\frac{2}{n^{c}A}, (207)

where in (i)(i) we used that j​ln⁡(n/j)≥ln⁡nj\ln(n/j)\geq\ln n for n>5n>5 and 1≤j≤n/51\leq j\leq n/5. The proof of [24, Lemma 18] then goes through otherwise unchanged, and we conclude that for any c>0c>0, and for sufficiently large nn and 𝔠1>0\mathfrak{c}_{1}>0,

ℙ⁡[Ω1]≥1−2nc−2​e−n−2​e−Tk∗n​A.\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{1}]\geq 1-\frac{2}{n^{c}}-2e^{-n}-2e^{-\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}. (208)

This concludes the analysis of f^0\hat{f}_{0}.

Step 2: Bounding |ℰ⁡(f^ℓ,f)||\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{\ell},f)|

Recall (11) and let ℰ(ℓ):=ℰ⁡(f^ℓ,f)\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}\vcentcolon=\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{\ell},f) for ℓ∈ℕ\ell\in\mathbb{N} (recall (11)). (211)

[24, Proposition 21] implies that the well-behaved contexts in ℋ\mathcal{H} are eventually classified correctly by Algorithm 5. Specifically, |ℰℋ(⌈ln⁡n​A⌉)|=0|\mathcal{E}^{(\lceil\ln nA\rceil)}_{\mathcal{H}}|=0 with high probability as n→∞n\rightarrow\infty. Meanwhile, [24, Proposition 20] bounds the number of contexts that are not in ℋ\mathcal{H}, therefore bounding |ℰℋc(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{c}}}|. We separately inspect these two results to obtain a bound on the probability with which their implications hold.

Step 2(a): Bounding |ℰℋc(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{c}}}|

We first inspect the proof of [24, Proposition 20] to derive a bound for |ℰℋc(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{c}}}|. In the process, we explain how the results of [24] can be refined to hold for η\eta-reachable and ℐ\mathcal{I}-identifiable BMDPs.

Step 2(b): Bounding |ℰℋ(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|

Ω5(ℓ):={|ℰ(ℓ)|n≤𝔠3n​S​ATk∗},\displaystyle\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\vcentcolon=\biggl\{\frac{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}|}{n}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{3}\sqrt{\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}}\biggr\},

Ω7:=⋂x{max{∑aN^k∗+1(x,a,[n]),∑aN^k∗+1([n],a,x)}≤𝔠5Tk∗n},\displaystyle\Omega_{7}\vcentcolon=\bigcap_{x}\biggl\{\max\biggl\{\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}(x,a,[n]),\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}([n],a,x)\biggr\}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{5}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\biggr\},

where the constants 𝔠3,𝔠4,𝔠5>0\mathfrak{c}_{3},\mathfrak{c}_{4},\mathfrak{c}_{5}>0 are chosen as follows.

Firstly, take 𝔠3\mathfrak{c}_{3} large enough that Ω1⊂Ω5(0)\Omega_{1}\subset\Omega_{5}^{(0)}, where we recall that ℰ(0)=ℰ⁡(f^0,f)\mathcal{E}^{(0)}=\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{0},f).

Secondly, note from (203) that [24, Proposition 24] bounds ℙ⁡[Ω6c]\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{6}^{\mathrm{c}}] for sufficiently large 𝔠4\mathfrak{c}_{4}. Take 𝔠4\mathfrak{c}_{4} large enough that [24, Proposition 24] applies.

Lastly, we claim that ℙ⁡[Ω7]\mathbb{P}[\Omega^{7}] can be bounded for sufficiently large 𝔠5\mathfrak{c}_{5} using [24, Lemma 17]. Given this claim, take 𝔠5\mathfrak{c}_{5} large enough so that [24, Lemma 17] applies.

To justify the claim, observe from (39) that ∑aN^k∗+1​([n],a,x)\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}([n],a,x) and ∑aN^k∗+1​(x,a,[n])\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}(x,a,[n]) count the number of transitions to and from a context xx in k∗k^{*} episodes, respectively. Since these differ by at most one visit per episode (when xx is one of the end points of an episode) it follows that

∑aN^k∗+1​([n],a,x)≤∑aN^k∗+1​(x,a,[n])+k∗almost surely.\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}([n],a,x)\leq\sum_{a}\hat{N}_{k^{*}+1}(x,a,[n])+k^{*}\quad\textnormal{almost surely}. (225)

Finally, recall that Γa=[n]\Gamma_{a}=[n] for a∈[A]a\in[A] by reduction (2). Together with (203), these observations prove that [24, Lemma 17] bounds ℙ⁡[Ω7c]\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{7}^{\mathrm{c}}] for sufficiently large 𝔠5\mathfrak{c}_{5}.

The following lemma summarizes the intermediate result that we require from the proof of [24, Proposition 21] to bound |ℰℋ(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|. It is proven in Section D.2.1.

Lemma D.2.

Assume Φ\Phi is η\eta-reachable and ℐ\mathcal{I}-identifiable, and that Tk∗=ω⁡(n​S3​A)T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nS^{3}A). Then there exist constants 𝔫1,𝔠5>0\mathfrak{n}_{1},\mathfrak{c}_{5}>0 such that for n>𝔫1n>\mathfrak{n}_{1}, ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, on Ω1∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7},

Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|≤𝔠5​(Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|+CLOSE|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|​Tk∗​An+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​(ln⁡Tk∗n)2OPEN+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​S​A​(|ℰ(ℓ)|n​Tk∗n​A+S​Tk∗n​A)).\begin{split}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|\leq\mathfrak{c}_{5}\biggl(\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|+&\sqrt{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}||\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|\frac{T_{k^{*}}A}{n}}+|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|\bigl(\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\bigr)^{2}\\ &+|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|SA\Bigl(\frac{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}|}{n}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}+S\sqrt{\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}\Bigr)\biggr).\end{split} (226)

Recall that Ω1\Omega_{1} and Ω4\Omega_{4} were defined in (204) and (222), respectively. In the remainder of this section we will use Lemma D.2 to prove that if Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)), then for sufficiently large nn,

Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂{|ℰℋ(⌈ln⁡n⌉)|=0}.\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\lceil\ln n\rceil)}|=0\}. (227)

[24, Appendix G.2] and [45, 35] perform similar analyses, proving that |ℰℋ(⌈ln⁡n⌉)|=0|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\lceil\ln n\rceil)}|=0 with high probability as n→∞n\rightarrow\infty in their settings. However, we must carefully keep track of the events and conditions for which |ℰℋ(⌊ln⁡n⌋)|=0|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\lfloor\ln n\rfloor)}|=0, so that we can ultimately obtain an explicit bound on the probability of this event. Our analysis therefore deviates from that of [24], such that the remainder of this section can be read independently of [24].

Assume that Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)). Our first step is to show that there exists 𝔫2>0\mathfrak{n}_{2}>0 such that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ+1)∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell+1)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}.

Since Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)) there exist 𝔫3,𝔠6>0\mathfrak{n}_{3},\mathfrak{c}_{6}>0 such that for n>𝔫3n>\mathfrak{n}_{3} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, on Ω4\Omega_{4},

|ℰℋc(ℓ)|/n≤𝔠6​n​S​A/Tk∗.|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{c}}}|/n\leq\mathfrak{c}_{6}\sqrt{nSA/T_{k^{*}}}. (228)

It therefore suffices to prove that there exists 𝔫2≥𝔫3\mathfrak{n}_{2}\geq\mathfrak{n}_{3} such that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, on Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7},

|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|≤|ℰℋ(ℓ)|.|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell+1)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\leq|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}|. (229)

Let ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0. Assume Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7} holds and that n>𝔫1n>\mathfrak{n}_{1}, where 𝔫1\mathfrak{n}_{1} is as in Lemma D.2. If ℰℋ(ℓ+1)=0\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}=0 there is nothing left to prove. Hence, also assume that ℰℋ(ℓ+1)>0\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}>0.

Lemma D.2 now implies (226). Dividing both sides of (226) by (Tk∗/n)​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|(T_{k^{*}}/n)\allowbreak|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|, we conclude that

1≤𝔠5​(|ℰℋ(ℓ)|n+|ℰℋ(ℓ)||ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​n​ATk∗+nTk∗​(ln⁡Tk∗n)2+n​S​ATk∗​(|ℰ(ℓ)|n​Tk∗n​A+S​Tk∗n​A)).1\leq\mathfrak{c}_{5}\biggl(\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{n}+\sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|}\frac{nA}{T_{k^{*}}}}+\frac{n}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggl(\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\biggr)^{2}+\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggl(\frac{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}|}{n}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}+S\sqrt{\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}\biggr)\biggr). (230)

Moreover, on Ω5(ℓ)\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}, (230) implies that

1≤𝔠5​(𝔠3​n​S​ATk∗+CLOSEOPEN|ℰℋ(ℓ)||ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​n​ATk∗+nTk∗​(ln⁡Tk∗n)2+n​S​ATk∗​(𝔠3​n​S​ATk∗​Tk∗n​A+S​Tk∗n​A)).\begin{split}1\leq\mathfrak{c}_{5}\biggl(\mathfrak{c}_{3}\sqrt{\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}}+&\sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|}\frac{nA}{T_{k^{*}}}}+\frac{n}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggl(\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\biggr)^{2}+\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggl(\mathfrak{c}_{3}\sqrt{\frac{nSA}{T_{k^{*}}}}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}+S\sqrt{\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}\biggr)\biggr).\end{split} (231)

Given that Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)), all terms on the right-hand side of (231) are o⁡(1)o(1) except possibly (n​A/Tk∗)​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|/|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|\sqrt{\smash[b]{(nA/T_{k^{*}})|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|/|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|}}. We therefore conclude that there exist constants 𝔠7>0\mathfrak{c}_{7}>0 and 𝔫4>𝔫3\mathfrak{n}_{4}>\mathfrak{n}_{3}, both independent of ℓ\ell, such that for n>𝔫4n>\mathfrak{n}_{4}, (n​A/Tk∗)​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|/|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|≥𝔠7\sqrt{\smash[b]{(nA/T_{k^{*}})|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|/|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|}}\geq\mathfrak{c}_{7}. |ℰℋ(ℓ+1)||ℰℋ(ℓ)|≤𝔠72​n​ATk∗.\frac{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell+1)}_{\mathcal{H}}|}{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}|}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{7}^{2}\frac{nA}{T_{k^{*}}}. (232)

Since Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)) it follows that there exists a constant 𝔫5>𝔫4\mathfrak{n}_{5}>\mathfrak{n}_{4} independent of ℓ\ell such that |ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|≤|ℰℋ(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell+1)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\leq|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}| almost surely. We have therefore established that there exists 𝔫2=𝔫3∨𝔫5\mathfrak{n}_{2}=\mathfrak{n}_{3}\vee\mathfrak{n}_{5} such that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0,

Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ+1)∩Ω6∩Ω7.\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell+1)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}. (233)

We can now iterate (233) to conclude that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2},

Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(0)∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂Ω1∩Ω4∩(∩ℓ≥0Ω5(ℓ))∩Ω6∩Ω7.\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(0)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap(\cap_{\ell\geq 0}\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)})\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}. (234)

Recall also that we assumed 𝔠3\mathfrak{c}_{3} in (204) is large enough that Ω1⊂Ω5(0)\Omega_{1}\subset\Omega_{5}^{(0)}. Together, these observations imply that

Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(0)∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂Ω1∩Ω4∩(∩ℓ≥0Ω5(ℓ))∩Ω6∩Ω7.\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(0)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap(\cap_{\ell\geq 0}\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)})\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}. (235)

Finally, recall that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, (232) holds on Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}. Since |ℰℋ(ℓ)|≤n|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\leq n for ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, it follows from (235) that for n>𝔫2n>\mathfrak{n}_{2}, on Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω6∩Ω7\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7},

|ℰℋ(⌈ln⁡n⌉)|≤(𝔠72​n​ATk∗)⌈ln⁡n⌉​|ℰℋ(0)|≤n​(𝔠72​n​ATk∗)ln⁡n=n​(1n)ln⁡(Tk∗𝔠72​n​A).|\mathcal{E}^{(\lceil\ln n\rceil)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\leq\biggl(\mathfrak{c}_{7}^{2}\frac{nA}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggr)^{\lceil\ln n\rceil}|\mathcal{E}^{(0)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\leq n\biggl(\mathfrak{c}_{7}^{2}\frac{nA}{T_{k^{*}}}\biggr)^{\ln n}=n\biggl(\frac{1}{n}\biggr)^{\ln\bigl(\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{\mathfrak{c}_{7}^{2}nA}\bigr)}. (236)

Because Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)) there exists 𝔫6>𝔫2\mathfrak{n}_{6}>\mathfrak{n}_{2} such that for n>𝔫6n>\mathfrak{n}_{6} the right-hand side of (236) is strictly less than 1. (227) finally follows for n>𝔫6n>\mathfrak{n}_{6} because ℰℋ(⌈ln⁡n⌉)∈ℕ\mathcal{E}^{(\lceil\ln n\rceil)}_{\mathcal{H}}\in\mathbb{N}.

Combining the bounds

Using |ℰ(ℓ)|=|ℰℋ(ℓ)|+|ℰℋc(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}|=|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}|+|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{c}}}| and f^alg=f^⌈ln⁡n⌉\hat{f}^{\textnormal{alg}}=\hat{f}_{\lceil\ln n\rceil}, together with (222) and (227), we find that for all sufficiently large nn,

Ω1∩Ω4∩Ω6∩Ω7⊂{|ℰ(⌈ln⁡n⌉)|=0}={f^alg=f}.\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{4}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}\subset\{|\mathcal{E}^{(\lceil\ln n\rceil)}|=0\}=\{\hat{f}^{\textnormal{alg}}=f\}. (237)

Recall also from the discussion following (224) that 𝔠4\mathfrak{c}_{4} in (224) is assumed large enough that [24, Proposition 24] bounds ℙ⁡[Ω6c]\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{6}^{\mathrm{c}}] and that 𝔠5\mathfrak{c}_{5} is assumed large enough that [24, Lemma 17] bounds ℙ⁡[Ω7c]\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{7}^{\mathrm{c}}]. Together with (204) and (223), we find that for all sufficiently large nn,

ℙ[f^alg=f]≥(237)ℙ[Ω1∩Ω3∩Ω6∩Ω7]≥1−2nc−2​e−n−2​e−Tk∗n​A−n⁡(S−1)​e−C​Tk∗n​ℐ′−2​e−18​Tk∗n​ln⁡Tk∗n−4​e−2​n​(1−ln⁡2)−2​e−Tk∗n​A.\begin{split}&\mathbb{P}[\hat{f}^{\textnormal{alg}}=f]\overset{\eqref{eqn:inclusion_perfect_clustering}}{\geq}\mathbb{P}[\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{3}\cap\Omega_{6}\cap\Omega_{7}]\\ &\geq 1-\frac{2}{n^{c}}-2e^{-n}-2e^{-\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}-n(S-1)e^{-C\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\mathcal{I}^{\prime}}-2e^{-\frac{1}{8}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}}-4e^{-2n(1-\ln 2)}-2e^{-\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}.\end{split} (238)

The right-hand side is 1−O⁡(1/nc)1-O(1/n^{c}) when Tk∗=ω⁡(n​A​(S3∨ln⁡n))T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nA(S^{3}\vee\ln n)). Proposition 5.3 follows from this. ∎

D.2.1 Proof of Lemma D.2

The following proof refers to results in [24, Appendices G.2 and G.4]. Note that the quantity e(ℓ)e^{(\ell)} appearing therein equals |ℰℋ(ℓ)||\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}_{\mathcal{H}}|. Recall also that ℰℋ(ℓ)=ℰ(ℓ)∩ℋ\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}=\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}\cap\mathcal{H} where ℰ(ℓ)=ℰ⁡(f^ℓ,f)\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}=\mathcal{E}(\hat{f}_{\ell},f) and ℋ\mathcal{H} is as in (209) and (210). Finally, recall the quantity ℒℓ​(x,s)\mathcal{L}_{\ell}(x,s) calculated by the improvement algorithm; see Section A.2.

With the identifications in (203), recall for ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0 the following quantity from [24, (86)]:

E≡E(ℓ):=∑x∈ℰℋ(ℓ+1)[ℒℓ​(x,f^ℓ+1​(x))−ℒℓ​(x,f⁡(x))].E\equiv E^{(\ell)}\vcentcolon=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}}[\mathcal{L}_{\ell}(x,\hat{f}_{\ell+1}(x))-\mathcal{L}_{\ell}(x,f(x))]. (239)

Here, we have corrected a typographical error appearing in [24, (86)] by replacing ℰℋ(ℓ)\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)} with ℰℋ(ℓ+1)\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}. This rectification ensures the claims (i) E(ℓ)≥0E^{(\ell)}\geq 0 and (ii) E(ℓ)=E1(ℓ)+E2(ℓ)+U(ℓ)E^{(\ell)}=E_{1}^{(\ell)}+E_{2}^{(\ell)}+U^{(\ell)} from [24] are true, with E1(ℓ)E^{(\ell)}_{1} and E2(ℓ)E^{(\ell)}_{2} defined in [24, (87)–(89)] and U(ℓ):=E(ℓ)−E1(ℓ)−E2(ℓ)U^{(\ell)}\vcentcolon=E^{(\ell)}-E^{(\ell)}_{1}-E^{(\ell)}_{2}; see also the explaining paragraph preceding [35, (35)]. Together, claims (i) and (ii) imply that −E1(ℓ)≤E2(ℓ)+|U(ℓ)|-E^{(\ell)}_{1}\leq E^{(\ell)}_{2}+|U^{(\ell)}|.

To prove Lemma D.2 it now suffices to show that if Tk∗=ω⁡(n​S3​A)T_{k^{*}}=\omega(nS^{3}A), then there exist constants 𝔫1,𝔠8,𝔠9,𝔠10>0\mathfrak{n}_{1},\mathfrak{c}_{8},\mathfrak{c}_{9},\mathfrak{c}_{10}>0 such that for n>𝔫1n>\mathfrak{n}_{1} and ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0, the following holds on Ω1∩Ω5(ℓ)∩Ω6\Omega_{1}\cap\Omega_{5}^{(\ell)}\cap\Omega_{6}:

−E1(ℓ)≥𝔠8​Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|,\displaystyle-E^{(\ell)}_{1}\geq\mathfrak{c}_{8}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|, (240)
E2(ℓ)≤𝔠9​(Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​ℰℋ(ℓ)|Tk∗​An+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​(ln⁡Tk∗n)2),\displaystyle E^{(\ell)}_{2}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{9}\biggl(\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|+\sqrt{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|\frac{T_{k^{*}}A}{n}}+|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell+1)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\biggl(\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\biggr)^{2}\biggr), (241)
|U(ℓ)|≤𝔠10​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​S​A​(|ℰ(ℓ)|n​Tk∗n​A+S​Tk∗n​A).\displaystyle|U^{(\ell)}|\leq\mathfrak{c}_{10}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|SA\biggl(\frac{|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell)}|}{n}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}+S\sqrt{\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{nA}}\biggr). (242)

This would then imply (226) for sufficiently large 𝔠5>0\mathfrak{c}_{5}>0.

We first consider the term E1(ℓ)E_{1}^{(\ell)}. Let ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0. It follows from the proof of [24, Lemma 21] that

−E1(ℓ)≥14​η2​Tk∗n​∑x∈ℰℋ(ℓ+1)I⁡(x,Φ)≥minx⁡I⁡(x,Φ)4​η2​Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|.-E^{(\ell)}_{1}\geq\frac{1}{4\eta^{2}}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}}I(x;\Phi)\geq\frac{\min_{x}I(x;\Phi)}{4\eta^{2}}\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|. (243)

It then follows from Lemma 5.1 that for η\eta-reachable and ℐ\mathcal{I}-identifiable BMDPs, minx⁡I⁡(x,Φ)/4​η2≥𝔠8\min_{x}I(x;\Phi)\allowbreak/4\eta^{2}\geq\mathfrak{c}_{8} for some constant 𝔠8>0\mathfrak{c}_{8}>0 that is independent of ℓ\ell. This gives (240).

Next, the proof of [24, Lemma 21] also demonstrates that there exists a constant 𝔠9>0\mathfrak{c}_{9}>0 such that on Ω1\Omega_{1},

E2(ℓ)≤𝔠9​(Tk∗n​|ℰℋ(ℓ)|n​|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​ℰℋ(ℓ)|Tk∗​An+|ℰℋ(ℓ+1)|​(ln⁡Tk∗n)2).E_{2}^{(\ell)}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{9}\biggl(\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\frac{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|}{n}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|+\sqrt{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell+1)}|\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{H}}^{(\ell)}|\frac{T_{k^{*}}A}{n}}+|\mathcal{E}^{(\ell+1)}_{\mathcal{H}}|\biggl(\ln\frac{T_{k^{*}}}{n}\biggr)^{2}\biggr). (244)

The event Ω1\Omega_{1} is used in the proof of [24, Lemma 21] when [24, Proposition 19] is invoked, which implies that Ω1\Omega_{1} holds with high probability as n→∞n\rightarrow\infty. This observation also demonstrates that 𝔠9\mathfrak{c}_{9} does not depend on ℓ\ell, therefore implying (241).

We conclude by proving (242). The corresponding bound in [24, Lemma 21] and its proof contain two typographical errors. Though these ultimately do not affect the conclusions of [24], correcting them is important for us to identify the event on which (242) holds. We therefore carry out the proof of (242) in more detail, while nonetheless leveraging intermediate results from the proof of [24, Lemma 21] when convenient.
